THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 101

Woe! to the inhabitants of Jerusalem!" After several of the class had tried it, Bill Suddith, who was a member of the class, looking very wise and dignified, ran the experiment. Montgomery said, "William, you sounded like you were trying to stop a hog."

Bill answered innocently, "Well, they do pretty much the same way."

Montgomery, seeing his signal, remarked, "William, can you beat that rendition of it?"

Bill replied, "Yes, Sir."

Montgomery challenged, "Then let us hear it." Bill arose and commenced with a ring of inflection on each "Woe" and delivered his recitation with a tremendous voice and a dramatic finish that brought down the house, and was given a sound thrashing. This was duly written to the episode of the scholar in The Platonian Messenger.

THE INIMITABLE PROFESSOR HOLLAND—Miss Lou Montgomery, writing in a commemorative tribute on Holland in the 1937 Anniversary Edition of The Savoy Star touches on a particular individual with characteristic Holland.

Mr. Holland was a man of a tranquil, philosophic mentality; not given to magnification of the law in its sternest aspects; free from bluster, stern, excitability, peculiar tribe, unreasonable expectations and petty grievances. He had a happy faculty of getting along with students one day, and that easily might have terminated in looking out of the room just once took his place, sat quite calmly in his chair, had him seated in the school one day, and as members of a family helped some students towards a better form of life—a way of taking their lessons easily, and as all members of a family helped some students their afternoon time well-scheduled in advance.

"Scott's Political Works, by the Ordnance" as it may be called, appeared in four issues from—Savoy, Bonham, Sherman, books for a dozen or an occasional student's way with only an occasional reference to the company.
